synopsis: CARLA is a free, MIT-licensed, Unreal-based driving simulator used for scene, sensor and closed-loop simulation; mining-interaction research has explored CARLA and ROS as a route from simulation to small-scale and physical testing [f15900, f15928, f397, f3488]. It has two release lines: 0.10.0, released on 19 December 2024, moved to Unreal Engine 5.5 and added native ROS 2 support and a mining earth-mover asset, while 0.9.16, released on 16 September 2025, remained on Unreal Engine 4 and added neural reconstruction capabilities [f8463, f8464, f8465, f8466, f8298]. Its off-road suitability remains unqualified: it lacks native deformable terrain or soil physics, was not found validated for off-road collision warning, and a 2026 mining-dust framework tuned to real lidar data did not have a confirmed simulated-versus-real point-cloud comparison [f8476, f5851, f4742, f4743]. The chapter 11 statement that no off-road sensor evidence was found is in tension with chapter 6's mining-lidar framework, although tuning alone does not establish validation [f9083, f4655, f4743]. The UE5 build requires Ubuntu 22.04 or Windows 11, at least an RTX 3000-series GPU with 16 GB VRAM, and 130 GB of disk; a frozen, qualified build is recommended because of release changes and installation, content and version friction [f8469, f15938, f8474]. An open-source chain can minimize license costs but demands substantial internal labor, with Chrono proposed for machine dynamics and terrain; frame rates and physics-based ultrasonic simulation were not found for CARLA, and project maintenance funding and security-patch cadence were not examined [f16128, f16158, f4957, f8547, f9392, f9393].
